close_reason: Fixed: doc updated to not overpromise
description:
pkix-identity/src/lib.rs line 246: The doc for `ServerName::to_owned` says 'avoids the intermediate clone when the inner data is borrowed', but the DNS arm does `cow.clone().into_owned()` — which when the cow is `Cow::Owned(String)` performs a String clone followed by a no-op move. The doc-claimed advantage over `.clone().into_owned()` on the struct doesn't exist: both paths do exactly one allocation regardless.

Same issue for `MailboxName::to_owned` (line 408).

The methods are correct and their total allocation count is fine (one per call). The doc comment just overpromises. Suggest simplifying the doc to 'Equivalent to `.clone().into_owned()`' (which the MailboxName doc already says), or using `Cow::Owned(cow.as_ref().to_owned())` which is genuinely cheaper in the already-owned case (avoids cloning the String).
title: ServerName::to_owned doc claim contradicts implementation
